item.title: Physical-Risk-Aware Decentralized Agents for Constrained Vehicle Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.17456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decentralized V2X resource control is challenging because each vehicle has only local observations, while reliability depends on network-wide interactions. We develop a physical-risk-aware spatio-temporal graph attention (PA-STGAT) framework for agentic V2X control. Each vehicle perceives its local interaction graph, retains short-term temporal context, and independently selects its PC5 resource and power. Network outcomes are used during centralized training to refine the shared policy. Transmitter-specific credits map reliability failures to individual vehicles. A dual-priced graph term further converts network violations into coordination signals for discrete resource selection, with higher priority on short time-to-collision links. Experiments show higher raw-policy reliability than the tested graph-based baselines. Under filtered execution, PA-STGAT meets the nominal empirical communication requirements across all five seeds, with tradeoffs among utility, delivery reliability, resource occupancy, and filter-induced repair. Compared with GNN+MATD3, it requires fewer resource repairs but achieves lower utility and mean delivery reliability. Mechanism ablations show that removing dual-priced graph coordination causes resource-selection collapse. Density and mobility tests characterize the operating limits of empirical constraint satisfaction.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Peng, William Weijia Zheng, Hang Liu, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang

item.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
item.description: arXiv:2611.17654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.
item.dc:creator: Yunseob Tae, Jeongjae Lee, Songnam Hong

item.title: Brain-inspired Beam Selection for mmWave RIS Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.17666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beam selection at large passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) requires either full channel knowledge or beam training, both of which entail unwanted overhead. On the other hand, learned models that predict the optimal codeword from channels sampled at a few active elements avoid both, at the cost of energy-demanding multiply-and-accumulate operations. In this paper, we propose spiking neural network (SNN)-based beam selection for a semi-active RIS assisting a mmWave multiple-input single-output communication system. Direct and sigmoid rate coding are compared against a multi- layer perceptron (MLP) of identical architecture. Energy analysis further reveals that the input layer dominates SNN energy consumption.
item.dc:creator: Aris Karampelas Timotijevic, Christos G. Tsinos, Alexandros-Apostolos A. Boulogeorgos, Theodoros A. Tsiftsis

item.title: Efficient Design of Flag Sequence Sets for Delay-Doppler Estimation via Riemannian Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.17673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter investigates the design of a Flag sequence set with peak-curtain auto-ambiguity functions to enable low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Given the predefined Curtain sequences, the Flag sequence set design problem is formulated as the minimization of the weighted integrated masked sidelobe level. To solve this problem, we first reformulate it as an unconstrained optimization problem on the unimodular manifold. Then, a tailored unimodular manifold conjugate gradient (UM-CG) algorithm is developed. Compared with the existing define algorithm, the proposed UM-CG algorithm reduces computational and storage requirements. Moreover, the global convergence of the proposed UM-CG scheme is theoretically derived under mild conditions. Numerical results demonstrate the superior optimization performance of the proposed UM-CG algorithm and show that the designed Flag sequences exhibit nearly ideal peak-curtain properties.
item.dc:creator: Xuyang Zhao, Zeping Sui, Zilong Liu, Jiangtao Wang, Yongchao Wang

item.title: Constant-Weight Sparse Vector Coded Augmented-AFDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.18013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse vector coding (SVC) and its variants convey information through sparse vectors (SVs), or sparse support patterns and detecting information by solving sparse recovery problems, making them attractive for short-packet ultra-reliable low-latency communications (URLLC). However, as the required information rate increases, conventional SVC schemes or the enhanced SVC (ESVC) schemes require a rapidly growing number of SVs, resulting in significant increase of complexity and receiver processing latency. On the other hand, when communicating in doubly selective channels, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) suffers from the Doppler spread induced inter-carrier interference, while affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) experiences the same peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) problem as OFDM, although it allows diversity gain from channel's double selectivity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a constant-weight sparse vector coded augmented AFDM (CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM ) scheme, along with a corresponding joint support and symbol detection algorithm. In this scheme, SVs are represented by constant-weight codewords that feature a fixed Hamming weight and a large Hamming distance, resulting in relatively small SV sets. Simulation results compare various SVC/ESVC schemes and diverse coding schemes employed by the CW-SVC/A$^2$FDM, including Hamming, BCH, RS, and polar codes, for QAM symbol protection. The results demonstrate that the proposed scheme provides a distinct reliability advantage over conventional SVC/ESVC schemes, achieving a gain of up to 14 dB. Furthermore, the study indicates that the CWC's weight and minimum Hamming distance must be carefully selected to balance detection reliability, QAM modulation order, and sparse recovery feasibility, thereby maximizing the overall system's performance.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Lu, Mohammed El-Hajjar, Lie-liang Yang

item.title: Recursive Semi-Blind Receivers for Wideband Array Processing
item.description: arXiv:2611.18039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the commonly employed uniform rectangular array (URA) as an illustrative example, we have recently shown that the block-term tensor decomposition (BTD) model provides a natural representation for the output signal of a multi-dimensional separable sensor array structure in the presence of channel multipath. A palette of effective and efficient semi-blind joint channel estimation/data detection (JCD) algorithms for URA processing, which wed BTD modeling with existing JCD schemes, has thus been developed, and recently extended so as to be applicable in large-scale arrays and/or time-varying environments. However, both the model and the algorithms were based on the assumption of narrowband signals, arriving through paths of effectively the same delay. In this paper, recursive JCD algorithms for wideband sources are developed and evaluated through simulations in a time-varying setting and across different constellation sizes, in comparison with their batch counterparts and the training-only-based solution. They are seen to enjoy the ability to track channel variations and detect the transmitted symbols `on the fly', with the aid of only a short initial training stage.
item.dc:creator: Eleftherios Kofidis

item.title: Dynamic Structural Causal Models for Delay Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.18155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic network key performance indicators (KPIs) such as end-to-end (E2E) delay are shaped by both contemporaneous interactions and temporal persistence. While standard predictors can forecast KPIs under a fixed regime, proactive network management requires reasoning about the effects of explicit actions (interventions) and, in time series, executing a model forward over multiple horizons. We study dynamic structural causal models (DSCMs) for E2E delay in a 5G measurement campaign, where payload and background traffic are intentionally manipulated and thus treated as do-interventions. We learn DSCM scaffolds using four time-series causal discovery methods representing score-based and constraint-based paradigms and common lag-based baselines. Using gradient-boosted decision trees, we evaluate true multi-step DSCM rollout, which recursively simulates the full system state, and a direct target-only ablation that predicts the KPI without recursive simulation. Across two held-out intervention scenarios, including high payload and 10 Mbps background traffic, we find that the inferred target parent/lag sets differ substantially across methods and that rollout behavior is strongly scenario-dependent. In particular, PCMCI+ achieves the best short-horizon rollout accuracy under the payload intervention (RMSE 2.97~ms) but exhibits pronounced horizon-dependent degradation under the background-traffic intervention (root mean squared error (RMSE) ~4.75 ms for long horizon), yielding a large positive rollout tax of up to ~0.78 ms relative to direct prediction; DyNoTEARS and VAR-based DSCMs remain comparatively stable under rollout. These results highlight that evaluating causal scaffolds only via direct prediction can be misleading, and therefore, executability under intervention and long-horizon error propagation are critical for DSCM-based KPI reasoning.
item.dc:creator: Niloofar Mehrnia, Wilson Ayyanthole Nelson, James Gross

item.title: Channel Prediction Using Deep Recurrent Neural Network with EVT-based Adaptive Quantile Loss Function
item.description: arXiv:2611.18171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultra-reliable low latency communication (URLLC) systems are pivotal for applications demanding high reliability and low latency, such as autonomous vehicles. In such contexts, channel prediction becomes essential to maintaining communication quality, as it allows the system to anticipate and mitigate the effects of fast-fading channels, thereby reducing the risk of packet loss and latency spikes. This letter presents a novel framework that integrates neural networks with extreme value theory (EVT) to enhance channel prediction, focusing on predicting extreme channel events that challenge URLLC performance. We propose an EVT-based adaptive quantile loss function that integrates EVT into the loss function of the deep recurrent neural networks (DRNNs) with gated recurrent units (GRUs) to predict extreme channel conditions efficiently. The numerical results indicate that the proposed GRU model, utilizing the EVT-based adaptive quantile loss function, significantly outperforms the traditional GRU. It predicts a tail portion of 7.26%, which closely aligns with the empirical 7.49%, while the traditional GRU model only predicts 2.4%. This demonstrates the superior capability of the proposed model in capturing tail values that are critical for URLLC systems.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Communications Letters, vol. 29, no. 7, pp. 1699-1703, July 2025
item.dc:creator: Niloofar Mehrnia, Parmida Valiahdi, Sinem Coleri, James Gross

item.title: Linear Dynamic Range Extension for Rydberg Atomic Receiver via Band-Limited Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.18181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg-atom receiver offers a promising approach to radio-frequency (RF) signal reception in wireless communication and sensing systems, combining high sensitivity with the potential for broad frequency coverage. However, the limited linear dynamic range (LDR) of the atomic system causes nonlinear distortion at high input signal levels, thereby restricting the receiver's effective linear input range. To address this issue, we analyze the mechanisms underlying nonlinear distortion in Rydberg atomic receivers and propose a physics-informed band-limited iterative reconstruction (PI-BLIR) method. Specifically, by exploiting the known nonlinear atomic response and signal bandwidth prior, we formulate a constrained maximum-likelihood problem to reconstruct the distorted complex intermediate-frequency (IF) waveform. With the bandwidth constraint absorbed into the frequency-domain parameterization, the constrained maximum-likelihood problem is transformed into an unconstrained optimization problem, which is solved using gradient descent. The proposed method relies solely on digital post-processing and requires no changes to the local-oscillator (LO) field strength, optical parameters, or atomic operating conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that PI-BLIR extends the receiver's LDR by more than 14 dB and enhances the demodulation performance of the atomic receiver.
item.dc:creator: Meng Fang, Lebin Chen, Jun-Rong Chen, Ming-Min Zhao, Bin-Bin Wei

item.title: How Robust are Pinching-Antenna Systems to Practical Deployment Imperfections?
item.description: arXiv:2611.18205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of pinching-antenna systems (PASSs) to three practical deployment imperfections: pinching-antenna (PA) positioning errors, imperfect channel state information (CSI), and line-of-sight (LoS) blockages. We develop analytical frameworks to quantify the performance degradation caused by each imperfection. For PA positioning errors, we employ a Brownian meander model to characterize the distribution and mean of the resulting signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) loss. The results show that positioning errors can diminish the gains from long-term position selection, with the loss becoming more pronounced under stronger shadow fading. For imperfect CSI, we characterize the distribution and moments of the true scattered channel power at the position selected using noisy channel estimates. The resulting selection penalty is governed by the ratio of noise variance to the number of channel measurements, while the upper tail of the selected channel power retains the same behavior as under perfect CSI. Finally, we develop a spatially consistent blockage model and derive the distribution of the optimum long-term SNR for arbitrary blockage configurations, together with a numerically tractable expression for a single blockage. Simulation results validate the analyses and highlight a fundamental property of PASSs: although positioning errors and imperfect CSI can reduce the gains from position selection, good performance can still be achieved provided that an LoS link is available. In particular, even when a large proportion of the waveguide is blocked, PA repositioning can establish LoS links and enable performance close to that of a fully unblocked system for the considered configurations.
item.dc:creator: Amy S. Inwood, Peter J. Smith, Hyundong Shin, Michail Matthaiou

item.title: Physical Prior Mismatch in Variational Dual-Polarization Quantum SATCOM Channel Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.18376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dual-polarization quantum satellite communications require accurate estimation of complex polarization channels. We investigate physical latent-prior mismatch in variational estimation of a $2\times 2$ complex channel, using eight Cartesian latent coordinates and a fixed latent-to-channel mapping. Gaussian, matched and sharpened Rician, Laplace, and Cauchy priors are compared under a fixed neural architecture and forward Kullback-Leibler objective. Models are trained for 300,000 updates with $\zeta=1/(2N_{\mathrm{est}})$ and evaluated using three training seeds and 10,000 shared held-out blocks per operating point. The Gaussian and Rician priors coincide at the Rayleigh limit. At higher Rician factors, the matched prior improves estimation accuracy, especially with fewer pilots. At $K=100$ and $N_{\mathrm{est}}=32$, the matched Rician variational estimator reduces mean squared Frobenius error by 2.50% relative to linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE). We also derive a joint Rician Bayesian posterior-mean estimator that incorporates the complete least-squares noise covariance and reduces posterior integration to one-dimensional quadrature. It improves on LMMSE by 3.33% at the same operating point and achieves lower observed error than the scalar Rician and both neural estimators at all 12 operating points. Additional Rician prior sharpening increases error, while Laplace and Cauchy controls remain near the Gaussian baseline.
item.dc:creator: Anders M. Buvarp, Stefan Werner

item.title: Joint Optimization of Antenna Partitioning and Distortion-Aware Precoding for Massive MIMO-OFDM with Peak Cancellation and In-Band Distortion Compensation
item.description: arXiv:2611.18405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In massive MIMO-OFDM systems, peak cancellation (PC) reduces the peak-to-average power ratio but introduces in-band distortion, where compensation signals transmitted from a subset of antennas can suppress this distortion at the users. However, their effectiveness depends on the antenna partition and compensation precoder, while nonlinear power amplifiers (PAs) generate additional distortion. This paper proposes a joint optimization method for antenna partitioning and distortion-aware compensation precoding. To enable this joint optimization, we derive a covariance-based analytical model of PC and PA distortion to predict the per-user, per-subcarrier signal-to-interference-plusdistortion- and-noise ratio (SIDNR). The predicted SIDNR is used to select the compensation precoder regularization, the disjoint antenna partition, and the number of compensation antennas. Numerical results demonstrate that joint optimization of the antenna partition and compensation precoder regularization improves BER and SIDNR-based spectral efficiency compared with fixed-partition designs, particularly at high signal-to-noise ratios.
item.dc:creator: Zhuoran Li, Osamu Muta, Haris Ga\v{c}anin

item.title: BladeSEI: A Multi-Channel and Multi-Day Dataset for Robust Specific Emitter Identification of Radars
item.description: arXiv:2611.18460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces "BladeSEI", a multi-channel receiver, multi-day dataset of radar pulses recorded over-the-air from 12 Software Defined Radios (SDRs) for the purpose of Specific Emitter Identification (SEI). The aim of this dataset is to enable investigation into robust SEI techniques that are able to generalise across different receiver channels and recording sessions. The dataset consists of two waveform types per emitter, a 50 microsecond chirped pulse of 40 MHz bandwidth and a 10 microsecond unmodulated pulse. Pulses are captured simultaneously on four synchronised analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) channels of a multi-channel receiver over three recording sessions on two days: a baseline session, an identical repeat on the following day, and a session in which the emitters were thermally conditioned to alter their operating temperature. Initial results using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Inception and ResNet based classifiers, trained and tested on a single ADC channel and recording session, show that the BladeRF emitters can be discriminated at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with ResNet achieving a macro-F1 above 0.98 at 25 dB for both waveforms, and performance degrading towards random guessing at 0 dB.
item.dc:creator: Ryan White, Robert Jones, Hassan Habib, Matthew A. Ritchie, Victoria Nockles, Adam Hosford

item.title: An All-Digital Coherent AFSK Demodulator for CubeSat Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.18509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio frequency-shift keying (AFSK) is a widely adopted modulation scheme for CubeSat systems due to its favorable bandwidth efficiency and implementation simplicity. However, coherent detection usually is avoided because synchronization impairments, caused by intense line-of-sight (LOS) dynamics inherent in low Earth orbit (LEO), may significantly degrade the bit error rate (BER). This paper presents a new all-digital coherent AFSK demodulator based on a Kalman filter (KF) for carrier phase and timing delay synchronization and the Viterbi algorithm for bit detection. The Viterbi algorithm is employed for maximum likelihood sequence detection, and the detected bit statistics are fed back to the KF to estimate phase shift, Doppler frequency shift, and Doppler drift induced by the LOS dynamics. Original mathematical analyses are derived to provide a theoretical foundation for the proposed demodulator's operation, specifically addressing its synchronization accuracy in dynamic LEO environments. The proposed demodulator is evaluated considering an additive white Gaussian noise channel with real CubeSat orbits. The performance results obtained through computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed model can withstand such scenarios with a gain of 5 dB in terms of BER compared to the conventional noncoherent AFSK demodulator. The KF performance is assessed using a moving root-mean-square error (MRMSE) statistic and the trace of its state error covariance matrix estimate.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Digital Signal Processing, vol. 162, art. no. 105147, 2025
item.dc:creator: Rubem Vasconcelos Pacelli, Rodrigo de Lima Florindo, Felix Antreich, Ant\^onio Macilio Pereira de Lucena

item.title: RF-Agent: A Practical Framework for Building Language Agents for RFIC Design
item.description: arXiv:2607.18772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have driven rapid progress in electronic design automation (EDA), yet their application to radio-frequency (RF) circuit design remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific datasets and standardized benchmarks. We present RF-Agent, which addresses this gap through textbook-driven knowledge distillation. A multi-agent Question-Thinking-Solution-Answer (QTSA) pipeline converts a subsection-level corpus from seven canonical RF textbooks into the first-of-its-kind RF-domain reasoning dataset (over 11,000 samples) with a dedicated multiple-choice benchmark. On this benchmark we study two adaptation strategies: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and three retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) configurations (semantic, keyword, hybrid). Across multiple LLM families, domain-specific SFT significantly improves RF reasoning, especially for small and medium-sized models; among RAG configurations, semantic retrieval performs best, indicating embedding-based context alignment suits RF reasoning better than naive fusion. The dataset and benchmark provide a reusable foundation for future work on LLM-aided RF circuit design.
item.dc:creator: Yueqi Xing, Houbo He, Jolie Wang, Erin Ni, Shikai Wang, Qiufeng Li, Weidong Cao, Taiyun Chi

item.title: Convergence Properties of PF-Exec: Homogeneous Structure, Anchored Closed Form, and Gain Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.17488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper establishes a layered mathematical char acterisation of PF-Exec, the algorithm of the companion system paper. Demand-proportional bandwidth allocation yields an exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, from which the equal-load bandwidth target and its feasibility bound follow in closed form. The logarithmic knee view preserves strict load order and shares its global optimum with the Jain fairness index, while the demand-weighted centroid minimises the position potential. The damped softmax association block possesses a fixed point on the product of simplices. The truncated one-dimensional gain iteration admits a complete characterisation, with geomet ric convergence below the critical gain, initial-value-dependent bounded oscillation at it, and a family of bounded two-state cycles above it. A global invariant error ball and an explicit tracking recursion complete the execution guarantee. A numerical audit confirms the structural identities on every measured state and quantifies the local amplification of the coupled association and resource dynamics. Together, the results explain how closed form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains provide stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Yiran Li, Yi Gao, Bo Ma

item.title: PF-Exec: Large-Scale UAV Relay Load Balancing with an Anchored Potential Direction Decider and a Per-Dimension Gain-Learning Executor
item.description: arXiv:2611.17492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relay load balancing in large-scale UAV networks requires joint decisions on association, bandwidth, power and hovering position, while the dimension grows with the number of UAVs and each UAV sees only its local state. This paper splits the decision into two layers. An anchored potential direction decider emits a closed-form target at every instant and returns its direction only. A gain-learning executor maps a local observation into a positive gain per dimension, composes gain and target, and clips the action against the physical single-step bound; the two layers form PF-Exec. The unit gain is the default start, so the executor reduces to the pure potential policy before training. The load is first-order homogeneous in bandwidth, making the bandwidth target closed form, and the position target is the demand-weighted centroid of the served users. The system uses a two-hop access and millimetre-wave backhaul link with soft association, a 3GPP UMa-AV channel with two shadowing layers, an OU-type social-force crowd and a quadrotor physical layer. Evaluation spans all fleet sizes, two crowd scenarios, independent seeds, the published baselines in their own settings and a degraded-information line. In the highest-pressure burst setting the fixed-step comparison breaks down on part of the seeds, losing fairness and mean load at once, while PF-Exec holds fairness near one. Among the ten comparison methods only the greedy heuristic survives that setting; its load variance stays far higher. Under stale global state and position noise the fairness index stays high at both largest-scale scenarios. Flight energy is nearly identical between the learned and the fixed-step executor, and three constants are fixed once across all settings. The convergence properties of both layers, from the truncated gain iteration to the perturbed tracking bound, are proved in the companion analysis.
item.dc:creator: Liheng Zeng, Hanzhang Jia, Yiran Li, Yi Gao, Bo Ma

item.title: uhd-rfsoc: Bringing Off-the-Shelf RFSoC Boards to Unmodified UHD Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.17723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Next-generation wireless research relies on software-defined radios (SDRs) with more channels and larger bandwidth. The USRP family is one of the most widely used SDR platforms, and much of the wireless software ecosystem is built on top of the USRP hardware driver (UHD). However, each USRP model comes with a fixed channel count, bandwidth, and streaming capability. Off-the-shelf radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) boards, on the other hand, integrate up to 16 analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and 16 digital-to-analog converters (DACs) operating at several gigasamples per second (GS/s), but existing UHD applications cannot directly use them. We present uhd-rfsoc, an open-source FPGA design and host software stack that turns these boards, including the 16-channel ZCU216 and the RFSoC 4x2, into standard UHD devices without modifying UHD. Through standard UHD calls, applications can configure the carrier frequency, channel count, the per-channel I/Q sample rate, and the wire format. uhd-rfsoc combines timestamped, flow-controlled sample transport in the FPGA with data plane development kit (DPDK) packet processing and vectorized sample conversion on x86 and Arm hosts. The built bitstreams for a number of RFSoC board configurations with varying RF data converter rates, channel counts, I/Q sample rates, and wire formats all successfully pass UHD's built-in streaming benchmarks. We further demonstrate compatibility with unmodified GNU Radio flowgraphs, a custom GPU-accelerated transceiver digital signal processing pipeline, as well as the OCUDU and Duranta 5G radio access network stacks using both software and commodity user equipment.
item.dc:creator: Wei Cheng, Yiming Li, Junyao Zheng, Cheng-Bin Chen, Tingjun Chen

item.title: A passive, battery-free flexible metasurface for implantable millimetre-wave radar glucose sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.17760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuous glucose monitors (CGM) break the skin barrier and require periodic sensor replacement. We investigated whether a passive, battery-free flexible metasurface, implanted beneath tissue and read by a commercial 60 GHz radar, can track blood glucose levels. The metasurface contained no electronics or reagents. We fitted a conical helix to the in-phase and quadrature radar signals across the frequency sweep and used its mean radius (the spiral radius) as the glucose-dependent feature. We tested glucose concentrations of 25 to 400 mg/dL in saline solution with and without the metasurface, and 196 to 596 mg/dL of total glucose in porcine whole blood beneath ex vivo porcine tissue and in a murine cadaver model with pulsatile blood flow. The metasurface was essential for achieving a monotonic sensor response; in saline, the coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of a logarithmic fit increased from 0.18 without the metasurface to 0.90 with it. In a murine (rat) cadaver model, the signal's spiral radius increased monotonically with glucose concentration despite pulsatile flow ($R^2$ = 0.91), and this monotonic behavior persisted through up to 6 mm of tissue. Although sensitivity decreased at higher glucose levels, each discrete concentration step remained clearly detectable. These results demonstrate that a shallow, passive implant paired with a commercial radar can effectively track blood glucose without requiring onboard electronics or batteries.
item.dc:creator: Kavya Saravanan, Rohini Ramachandran, Jean Pierre Ndabakuranye, Isabelle Shearer, Gursimran Singh, Bobbi Fleiss, Omid Kavehei, Akram Al-Hourani, Francisco J. Tovar Lopez, Margaret Lech, Arman Ahnood

item.title: Protection-Oriented Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Fault Detection in Power Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.17872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based fault detectors are increasingly proposed for power system protection, yet aggregate metrics can obscure the consequences of false and missed trips. We present a protection-oriented assessment of three ML detectors and a sequence-current reference on PROTECT-90, comprising 9,022 simulated fault episodes on a 90 kV double-circuit line. The assessment combines five window conditions, causal window-end labelling, episode-grouped cross-validation, and operating-point selection under a fixed security budget. It reports security, dependability, detection timing, decision margins, and episode-level nuisance assertions. Gradient-boosted trees, a convolutional neural network, and logistic regression achieve AUC-ROC values above 0.999, yet at a security budget of $10^{-3}$ their developed-fault missed-trip rates range from 0.007% to 1.99%. Post-clearing false-trip rates of approximately 0.12-0.16% per window coexist with nuisance assertions in 11.3-19.1% of episodes. Among the analysed physical descriptors, missed trips are most consistently associated with higher fault resistance within the sampled range. An analytical current proxy suggests a fault-current gradient only partly reproduced by waveform-derived current (rank correlation 0.62). No single topology state or faulted phase consistently dominates within the sampled domain. Because PROTECT-90 contains fault episodes only, security is assessed on pre-fault and post-clearing windows rather than independent non-fault disturbances.
item.dc:creator: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Changhun Kim, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

item.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation
item.description: arXiv:2611.17950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Separating a radio-frequency signal of interest from a co-channel interference is mostly addressed with specialized separators, each trained for one pair of signal and interference types and therefore relying on a label that a heavily jammed receiver cannot identify. We show that this reliance is not benign: applied to an interference it was not trained on, such a separator usually fails to recover the signal, and in most of the cases we measure it leaves the signal worse than no processing at all. We then train a single separator over every pair, giving it no indication at test time of which one it faces, on two architectures with no component in common: the convolutional WaveNet of the ICASSP 2024 RF Challenge, and a band-split transformer that we adapt from music source separation. Both behave the same way. At the size of one specialized model, the unified separator stays close to the whole models it replaces, keeping the bit error rate close on almost every pair, better on one and worse on another. On an interference absent from every training set, it does as well as the best specialized model, without anyone having to choose which one to deploy.
item.dc:creator: Maxence Albert, Rapha\"el Duroselle, Thibaud Ehret, Olivier Boeffard, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Bonastre

item.title: PTMTD: A Topology-Aware Temporal-Graph Attention Network for Joint Cyber-Attack Detection and Relay-Level Localization in Power System Protection Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.18184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The digitization of protection relays exposes power grids to sophisticated cyberattacks, yet existing GNN detectors omit temporal encoding, rely on static topologies, and lack relay localization. We propose PTMTD-a Pearson-driven Temporal Multimodal Topology-aware Detection Network-coupling a dilated TCN with multi-head GATv2 in a dual-head architecture for simultaneous 37-class detection and four-relay localization. PTMTD constructs its graph from measurement correlations (no impedance data) and is trained with a composite loss jointly optimizing both tasks. On the MSU-ORNL benchmark (78,377 samples, 37 classes), it achieves 99.27% accuracy, 99.25% macro F1, and 95.98% localization, outperforming GraphKAN, LSTM, GCN, and Random Forest by 5.64-11.15 percentage points (p < 0.05). Ablations confirm gains from temporal encoding (+2.38%), graph attention (+2.69%), residuals (+2.07%), and correlation-driven supervision. With 639k parameters and 2.5 ms CPU inference, PTMTD is lightweight and deployment-ready. While validated on a transmission testbed, the architecture applies to microgrids with similar relay structures. Code and models are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Shahin Razazni, Mohammad Ali Alirezapouri

item.title: DecompJSCC: Joint Source-Channel Coding With Decoupled SNR and Rate Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2611.18379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) for image transmission must adapt to changes in the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and available transmission resources. However, some existing joint-adaptive methods condition the encoder on the requested rate, while others apply static masks after encoding. The former couples latent formation to the rate request, whereas the latter cannot adapt channel selection to image content. To address these limitations, we propose DecompJSCC, which decomposes joint adaptation into SNR-conditioned latent formation and post-encoding rate control within a single model. The encoder applies SNR-conditioned block attention residuals across all stages, aggregating intra-stage and cross-stage semantic representations. At the receiver, an adapter performs SNR-conditioned affine correction. We introduce a post-encoding rate-adaptive channel semantic budgeting (RCSB) module whose shared gate selects channels of the formed latent by image content, adjusts their gains, and keeps exactly the requested count. This keeps the encoder output independent of the rate request for a fixed image and SNR. Experimental results show that DecompJSCC outperforms SwinJSCC and SA-RA-JSCC in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) across a range of SNR and rate settings, by 0.64 and 1.00 dB over SwinJSCC and by 0.97 and 0.96 dB over SA-RA-JSCC on Kodak and CLIC2021, while using only 7.5% of SwinJSCC's Adaptive ModNet parameters.
item.dc:creator: Yunhao Liu, Jiancun Fan, Haojun Sun, Jie Luo, Qing Zhao

item.title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
item.description: arXiv:2611.18434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity groups. We observed that the SleepXAI model achieves strong classification performance on both datasets. Among the evaluated methods, Integrated Gradients (IG) consistently achieves the highest mean attribution fidelity across all five sleep stages on Sleep-EDF and across all AHI groups on DREAMT, outperforming all other evaluated methods under the Spearman rank correlation metric. These findings highlight the importance of attribution method selection as a key factor for ensuring reliable and clinically interpretable automated sleep staging systems.
item.dc:creator: Gurinder Kaur Sandhu, Jude Koenig, Ankita Shukla, Shruti Kshirsagar

item.title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM
item.description: arXiv:2611.18450v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frequency-selective fading and oscillator phase noise (PN) jointly impair coded sub-THz OFDM reception. We propose a decoder-confidence-guided two-round receiver combining a {pilot-aware complex transformer} (PACT) estimator, banded linear minimum mean-square error equalization, and neural normalized min-sum decoding. PACT jointly estimates the frequency-domain channel and effective time-domain PN through interacting complex-valued branches. Decoder-derived pseudo-pilots and continuous constellation-aware confidence guide second-round refinement through PACT inputs and attention, with parameters shared across rounds. At $E_b/N_0=30$~dB, the PACT receiver achieves approximately $70\%$ and $57\%$ lower code-block error rates than the best-performing learning-based baseline in the two benchmark settings, respectively. Frozen-weight tests further demonstrate applicability across channel/PN models, carrier frequencies, and FFT/bandwidth configurations.
item.dc:creator: Ruilin Wang, Xiaodai Dong

item.title: Asymptotic Margins and Feature Confinement in Conic Classification Heads under Softmax Cross-Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.18507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. We ask whether these regions also keep the features bounded when the head is trained with softmax cross-entropy. For a head whose class scores combine a linear term with a Euclidean norm, we first show that the region of each class is bounded by a quadric of revolution, whose eccentricity is the reciprocal of one learned ratio. We then attach to each class an asymptotic margin, which compares the growth of its score with the growth of all the other scores and can be computed by a second-order cone program. The loss of a class has infimum zero exactly when its margin is positive, and it then approaches zero only along diverging features. When the margin is negative, the loss is coercive and its minimizers lie in an explicit ball. Since softmax depends only on the differences between scores, a class with a bounded region can still have a positive margin, so bounded regions do not confine the features. The result extends to other norms, including the polyhedral conic functions. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, all 1210 cells of 67 trained conic heads have positive margins, whereas a prototype head keeps nine of its ten cells bounded, as the theory predicts.
item.dc:creator: Omer Nezih Gerek

item.title: Multi-Band Sensing in FR3 with Background Dense Multipath Components
item.description: arXiv:2602.23539v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-band sensing has emerged as a key enabler of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), one of the six primary usage scenarios defined for IMT-2030 (6G). The introduction of frequency range 3 (FR3, 7-24 GHz), comprising non-contiguous sub-bands across a wide frequency span, further reinforces the importance of multi-band operation. In such scenarios, frequency-dependent propagation effects that are collectively referred to as dense multipath components (DMC), including clutter, diffraction, and diffuse scattering, must be carefully considered. Building on prior literature and our experimental observations, this paper proposes a novel ISAC channel analysis tailored to multi-band sensing, based on a channel model with background DMCs. It also assesses the sensing trade-offs among sub-bands by analyzing Cram\'er-Rao bound (CRB)-based fundamental limits. Furthermore, a scalable multi-band estimator is proposed that resolves angular ambiguities arising from the grating lobes effect. Simulation results of the multi-band estimator demonstrate substantial gains in estimation accuracy and reductions in false alarm rate over single-band estimators operating on each constituent sub-band within the CRB-achieving regime. In a representative test case, the proposed estimator achieves reductions of 37.41% and 17.04% in the root mean squared error of delay estimation compared to single-band estimators operating at 8.75 GHz and 21.7 GHz, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Dexin Wang, Roberto Bomfin, Ahmad Bazzi, Marwa Chafii

item.title: Timing-Aware Satellite Association for Multi-LEO Direct-to-Handset Communications
item.description: arXiv:2603.03729v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rapid deployment of large-scale low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations has positioned direct-to-handset (D2H) communications as a key enabler of future non-terrestrial networks. However, the limited link budget of handheld devices makes broadband service delivery challenging, and multi-satellite cooperative transmission is often required to provide sufficient power gain. In practice, such cooperation is severely hindered by asynchronous reception across satellites. This paper analyzes the received-signal model under the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) transmitter structure and shows that satellite-dependent propagation delays prevent simultaneous timing alignment for multiple user terminals (UTs). This timing mismatch induces severe inter-carrier interference (ICI) and inter-symbol interference (ISI), even from the intended signals, which fundamentally constrains the achievable cooperative gain. To address this issue, we propose a timing-aware satellite association strategy that enables cooperation only with satellites expected to satisfy a UT-side timing tolerance, thereby avoiding dominant asynchronous interference by design. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy improves throughput performance compared to single-satellite transmission and fully connected multi-satellite baselines.
item.dc:creator: Hyunwoo Lee, Incheol Hwang, Daesik Hong

item.title: Multi-Objective Adaptive Beamforming Using Partial Knowledge of Dynamic Dielectric Media for Non-Invasive Microwave Hyperthermia
item.description: arXiv:2605.00215v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate multi-objective adaptive beamformer design strategies for non-invasive microwave hyperthermia. Our focus is to address the challenges of maintaining focused power deposition in desired locations while reducing unwanted heating elsewhere under conditions of changing dielectric properties. The process of heating the media causes changes in the dielectric properties of the media, which can degrade the effectiveness beamformers with static weights. Typical hyperthermic beamformer designs calculate antenna beamforming weights using patient-specific high resolution dielectric maps obtained by MRI or microwave tomography, however this process is time consuming and difficult to perform in real-time. In this work, we explore the efficacy of microwave hyperthermia in various inhomogeneous media under changing dielectric conditions, with the goal of informing the design of future adaptive real-time microwave hyperthermia techniques. We aim to achieve cell apoptosis by obtaining temperatures of $\sim$ 45 $^\circ\text{C}$ through selective absorption of electromagnetic wave focusing at a 2.5 GHz carrier frequency with little to no knowledge of the changes in the dielectric media and simultaneously place nulls to avoid unwanted heating outside of the treatment zone. We investigate the effectiveness of the linear constrained minimum power (LCMP) algorithm for near-field multi-objective beamforming and examine the power density obtained from finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations on simple analytical models and anatomically realistic numerical breast phantoms. To gain a comprehensive knowledge of the efficacy of the beamformer we evaluate the resulting thermal maps of the models in simple homogeneous cases, heterogeneous cases and MRI-derived phantom breast models.
item.dc:creator: Ahona Bhattacharyya, Tessa Haldes, Jeffrey A. Nanzer, Susan C. Hagness

item.title: Sensing-Aided Beam Selection for UAV Networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.00277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fast and low-overhead beam management is essential for the practical deployment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication networks operating at millimeter-wave and higher frequencies. In this paper, we propose a radar-assisted beam selection framework for UAV networks that exploits spatial sensing information, including angle-of-departure and distance estimates, to efficiently identify communication beams. Specifically, a digitally beamformed radar array with a relatively small number of antennas provides rapid, coarse UAV localization, while an analog-beamformed communication array, requiring fewer radio-frequency chains, exploits coarse localization to narrow the beam-search region and establish a communication link with the UAV. To provide theoretical insight into the expected overhead, we conduct a probabilistic analysis in which an approximation of the nearest-first beam selection overhead under idealized conditions is proposed and its statistics are derived for a Gaussian error model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed radar-assisted beam selection significantly reduces the number of beams that need to be examined, requiring on average at most 1.64 candidate beams even under per-element radar phase errors of up to 100{\deg}.
item.dc:creator: Bora Bozkurt, Ali Gorcin, Cevdet Tosun, Mehmet Nuri Akinci, Ibrahim Hokelek, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir

item.title: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting
item.description: arXiv:2610.13357v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, leaving patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking can embed this metadata in the signal, but conventional methods fail under time shifts, and high waveform similarity does not guarantee the same downstream diagnosis. We present \rev{ECGGuard}, a deep watermarking framework for single-lead ECG. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message frame by frame and checks for watermark presence, and during training a frozen arrhythmia classifier penalizes changes that would alter its predictions. Because high bit accuracy does not ensure whole-message recovery, the payload is protected by extended Hamming codes, \rev{a validation-selected channel ordering}, and soft-decision decoding. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, \rev{averaged over three training runs, ECGGuard} keeps bit accuracy above \rev{98\%} under time shifts of 10 to 50 samples, where transform-domain baselines drop to chance. The coded 16-bit payload is recovered exactly in \rev{99.95\%} of clean segments\rev{, in over 96\%} under time shifts, 10\% sample deletion, or 10\% packet loss\rev{, and in 99.1\% for unseen subjects}. \rev{For the guiding classifier, the diagnostic loss limits the drop in ventricular-beat sensitivity to 1.6 percentage points on the test records (35.0 without it) and to 12.2 points for unseen subjects (67.0 without it); the drop grows to 10.3 points for independently trained classifiers, and the protection does not transfer to an external database.} \rev{ECGGuard} has 0.56 million parameters and needs about \rev{19}~ms per segment on a desktop CPU.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Yu Chen, Kuan-Chen Wang, Yu Tsao, Jian-Jiun Ding

item.title: Beyond TR 38.811 for 6G NTN Channel Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.03869v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) expands 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) to S, Ku, and Ka bands for integration with existing terrestrial cellular networks, the necessary satellite channel model for link and network performance evaluation remains tied to TR 38.811, last revised in 2020. We identify issues on multiple fronts: inappropriate parameter specifications based on very limited site-specific environments considered, omission of satellite-induced Doppler spread and directional antenna effects and lack of a transparent channel model generation procedure. To address these limitations, we re-derive the channel parameters using ray tracing (RT) over urban and rural environments based on ITU-R building statistics. Our results show that TR 38.811 substantially overestimates the K-factor at low elevations and predicts a decreasing trend with elevation, which is inconsistent with RT. The Ka-band clutter loss (CL) also exceeds the RT estimates by more than 15 dB in urban cases. It also underestimates rural delay spread (DS) at low elevations and predicts an elevation trend inconsistent with RT. We further quantify the previously neglected satellite-induced Doppler spread. Finally, we demonstrate that the conventional TR 38.811 channel generator significantly underestimates the K-factor in the presence of directional antenna (beamforming), while our modified generator substantially reduces this discrepancy.
item.dc:creator: Kuan-Po Chiu, Aaron Jacob Buck, Sumit Roy

item.title: Auto-differentiable data assimilation: Co-learning of states, dynamics, and filtering algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2603.20891v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Data assimilation algorithms estimate the state of a dynamical system from partial observations, where the successful performance of these algorithms hinges on costly parameter tuning and on employing an accurate model for the dynamics. This paper introduces a framework for jointly learning the state, dynamics, and parameters of filtering algorithms in data assimilation through a process we refer to as auto-differentiable filtering. The framework leverages a theoretically motivated loss function that enables learning from partial, noisy observations via gradient-based optimization using auto-differentiation. We further demonstrate how several well-known data assimilation methods can be learned or tuned within this framework. To underscore the versatility of auto-differentiable filtering, we perform experiments on dynamical systems spanning multiple scientific domains, such as the Clohessy-Wiltshire equations from aerospace engineering, the Lorenz-96 system from atmospheric science, the generalized Lotka-Volterra equations from systems biology, and the two-layer quasi-geostrophic model from geophysical fluid dynamics. Finally, we provide guidelines for practitioners to customize our framework according to their observation model, accuracy requirements, and computational budget.
item.dc:creator: Melissa Adrian, Daniel Sanz-Alonso, Rebecca Willett

item.title: Analytically Characterized Optimal Power Control for Signal-Level-Integrated Sensing, Computing and Communication in Federated Learning
item.description: arXiv:2604.26741v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices' transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications, vol. 25, pp. 25941-25958, 2026
item.dc:creator: Paul Zheng, Yao Zhu, Xiaopeng Yuan, Yulin Hu, Anke Schmeink

item.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2610.03713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continual learning treats any drop in performance on previously seen data as forgetting, a convention inherited from settings where the prediction target is stationary. World models violate this assumption: their target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when learned can later become false, and revising it is correct behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but it has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode structural knowledge, such as physical laws and object permanence, that must never be degraded. We argue that continual world models need retention stratified by invariance timescale, the time over which knowledge stays true: invariants should be refined but never degraded, while instance-level facts should be revised once the environment changes. We show that standard forgetting metrics, used alone, count correct revision as forgetting and so rank a frozen model highest. We propose differential retention, which reports two quantities separately: invariant retention, checked after every adaptation round, and revision latency, the number of observations a model needs to pick up a change.
item.dc:creator: Nishit Anand, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha

item.title: Lightweight Semantic EEG Foundation Model for Frozen Cross-Disorder Transfer
item.description: arXiv:2610.05503v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large-scale EEG foundation models have demonstrated promising transferability across neurological disorders, but often require millions of parameters and substantial computational resources. In this paper, we present the Universal Semantic EEG Foundation Model (USE-FM), a lightweight EEG foundation model that learns transferable neural representations through self-supervised signal reconstruction on the Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus (TUEG). After pretraining, the encoder is frozen and evaluated on two clinically distinct downstream tasks, abnormal EEG detection (TUAB) and epileptic seizure recognition (TUEP), using a unified frozen-transfer protocol against recent EEG foundation models, including LUNA-Base and CBraMod. With only 1.46 million parameters, approximately one-fifth the size of existing models, USE-FM achieves competitive overall performance, including strong sensitivity and F1-score on TUEP (SEN $75.00 \pm 14.14$, F1 $70.37 \pm 4.01$), while maintaining competitive performance on TUAB (AUC $85.24 \pm 5.61$). Beyond downstream classification, latent representation analysis using $k$-means clustering together with PCA and t-SNE demonstrates that USE-FM learns organized semantic EEG representations comparable to substantially larger foundation models. These results suggest that large-scale self-supervised pretraining enables lightweight architectures to learn transferable semantic EEG representations, providing a computationally efficient foundation for cross-disorder analysis and future clinical decision support in neurological disorders.
item.dc:creator: Rita Huan-Ting Peng, Nhat Bui

item.title: Similar Predictive Fit but Different Latent Dynamics: Characterizing Learned Dynamical Structure in Personalized Models of Brain Disorders
item.description: arXiv:2610.10850v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As AI models move toward clinical decision-making and personalized treatment, understanding \emph{what} a model learns is important beyond predictive accuracy alone. We investigate whether personalized latent dynamics reveal clinically associated differences even when predictive fit is similar. A lightweight CNN--Transformer EEG foundation model pretrained on the Temple University EEG Corpus (TUEG) extracts segment-level representations. Using the Temple University Epilepsy Corpus (TUEP), representations are mapped to a shared latent-state space, and sparse multinomial logistic transition distributions (mLTD) are fit independently to each subject to obtain personalized transition-dependency graphs $W_n$. Analyses include $n{=}198$ subjects (99 epilepsy / 99 non-epilepsy). At $k{=}4$, epilepsy subjects exhibit substantially denser learned dependency structure ($p{=}1.1\times10^{-7}$), with the same pattern at $k{=}6$ (19.90 vs. 13.46; $p{=}5.2\times10^{-5}$). Graph-derived features provide moderate group discrimination under 5-fold subject-wise cross-validation (AUROC 0.68 at $k{=}4$; 0.65 at $k{=}6$). In contrast, held-out log-likelihood is nearly identical between groups at $k{=}4$ ($-0.992$ vs. $-0.991$; $p{=}0.95$), with similarly matched next-state prediction (AUROC 0.855 vs. 0.861; $p{=}0.54$). Thus, similar predictive fit does not imply similar learned dynamics: groups can be comparably predictable while differing substantially in the internal dynamical structure learned by personalized models. This distinction motivates evaluating learned structure alongside predictive performance in personalized clinical models.
item.dc:creator: Rita Huan-Ting Peng, Nhat Bui
